style="line-height:120%;padding-top:16px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Inventories of Materials and Supplies</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">Inventories are primarily replacement parts and supplies held for consumption in our drilling operations. Inventories are valued at the lower of cost or net realizable value. Cost is determined on a weighted average basis and includes the cost of materials, shipping, duties and labor. Net realizable value is defined as the estimated selling price in the ordinary course of business, less reasonably predictable costs of completion, disposal and transportation. The reserves for excess and obsolete inventory were </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$11.5 million</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> and </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$9.9 million</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> for fiscal years </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">2019</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> and </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">2018</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, respectively.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:16px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Investments</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">We maintain investments in equity securities of certain publicly traded companies. We recognize our marketable equity securities that have readily determinable fair values at fair value, with changes in such values reflected in net income. We adopted ASU No. 2016-01 on October 1, 2018, and as a result, we recognize our marketable equity securities that have readily determinable fair values at fair value, with changes in such values reflected in net income.&#160;Previously, we recognized changes in fair value of equity securities in other comprehensive income in the Consolidated Statements of Comprehensive Income (Loss). There is no longer a requirement to consider whether the decline in fair value is other-than-temporary. </span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:16px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Property, Plant, and Equipment</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">Property, plant and equipment are stated at cost less accumulated depreciation. Substantially all property, plant and equipment are depreciated using the straight-line method based on the estimated useful lives of the assets after deducting their salvage values. The amount of depreciation expense we record is dependent upon certain assumptions, including an asset&#8217;s estimated useful life,&#160;rate of consumption, and corresponding salvage value. We periodically review these assumptions and may change one or more of these assumptions. Changes in our assumptions may require us to recognize, on a prospective basis, increased or decreased depreciation expense.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">We capitalize interest on major projects during construction. Interest is capitalized based on the average interest rate on related debt. We had </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>no</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> capitalized interest for fiscal year </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">2019</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> and </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$0.4 million</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> and </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$0.3 million</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> of capitalized interest for </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">2018</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> and </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">2017</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, respectively.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">We review long-lived assets for impairment whenever events or changes in circumstances indicate that the carrying amount of an asset may not be recoverable.&#160;Changes that could prompt such an assessment include a significant decline in revenue or cash margin per day, extended periods of low rig asset group utilization, changes in market demand for a specific asset, obsolescence, completion of specific contracts, restructuring of our drilling fleet, and/or overall general market conditions.&#160;&#160;If the review of the long-lived assets indicates that the carrying value of these assets/asset groups&#160;is more than the estimated undiscounted future cash flows projected to be realized from the use of the asset and its eventual disposal&#160;an impairment charge is made, as required, to adjust the carrying value down to the estimated fair value of the asset.&#160;&#160;The estimated fair value is determined based upon either an income approach using estimated discounted future cash flows, a market approach considering factors such as recent market sales of rigs of other companies and our own sales of rigs, appraisals and other factors, a cost approach utilizing reproduction costs new as adjusted for the asset age and condition, and/or a combination of multiple approaches.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">Cash flows are estimated by management considering factors such as prospective market demand, margins, recent changes in rig technology and its effect on each rig&#8217;s marketability, any investment required to make a rig operational, suitability of rig size and make up to existing platforms, and competitive dynamics including industry utilization.&#160;Long-lived assets that are held for sale are recorded at the lower of carrying value or the fair value less costs to sell.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:16px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Goodwill and Intangible Assets</span></div><div value of net assets acquired in a business combination, at the date of acquisition. Goodwill is not amortized but is tested for potential impairment at the reporting unit level at a minimum on an annual basis in the fourth fiscal quarter of each fiscal year or when it is more likely than not that the carrying value may exceed fair value. If an impairment is determined to exist, an </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">impairment </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;color:#252525;">charge for the amount by which the carrying amount exceeds the reporting unit&#8217;s fair value is recognized, limited to the total amount of goodwill allocated to that reporting unit.&#160;&#160;The reporting unit level is defined as an operating segment or one level below an operating segment.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;color:#252525;">Finite-lived intangible assets are amortized </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">using</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;color:#252525;"> the straight-line method over the period in which these assets contribute to our cash flows, generally estimated to be </span><span policies for valuation of long-lived assets.&#160;</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:16px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Drilling style="line-height:120%;padding-top:16px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Income Taxes</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">Current income tax expense is the amount of income taxes expected to be payable for the current fiscal year.&#160;&#160;Deferred income taxes are computed using the liability method and are provided on all temporary differences between the financial basis and the tax basis of our assets and liabilities.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">We provide for uncertain tax positions when such tax positions do not meet the recognition thresholds or measurement standards prescribed in Accounting Standards Codification (&#8220;ASC&#8221;) 740,</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:9pt;"> </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Income Taxes</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, which is more fully discussed in </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">Note 8&#8212;Income Taxes</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">.&#160;&#160;Amounts for uncertain tax positions are adjusted in periods when new information becomes available or when positions are effectively settled.&#160;&#160;We recognize accrued interest related to unrecognized tax benefits in interest expense and penalties in other expense in the Consolidated Statements of Operations.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:16px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Earnings per Common Share</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">Basic earnings per share is computed utilizing the two-class method and is calculated based on the weighted-average number of common shares outstanding during the periods presented. Diluted earnings per share is computed using the weighted-average number of common and common equivalent shares outstanding during the periods utilizing the two-class method for stock options and nonvested restricted stock. We have granted and expect to continue to grant to employees restricted stock grants that contain non-forfeitable rights to dividends. Such grants are considered participating securities under ASC 260,&#160;</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Earnings Per Share</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">. As such, we have included these grants in the calculation of our basic earnings per share.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:16px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Stock-Based Compensation</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">Stock-based compensation expense is determined using a fair-value-based measurement method for all awards granted.&#160;During the fiscal year ended September&#160;30, 2019, there were no new non-qualified stock options granted, as we have, prospectively and for fiscal year 2019, replaced stock options with performance share units as a component of our executives&#8217; long-term equity incentive compensation. We have also eliminated stock options as an element of our director compensation program. The Board has determined to award stock-based compensation to directors solely in the form of restricted stock. </span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">The fair value of each option granted in prior years was estimated on the date of grant based on the Black-Scholes options-pricing model utilizing assumptions for a risk-free interest rate, volatility, dividend yield and expected remaining term of the awards.&#160;The assumptions used in calculating the fair value of stock-based payment awards represent management&#8217;s best estimates, but these estimates involve inherent uncertainties and the application of management judgment.&#160;</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">The grant date fair value of performance share units is determined through use of the Monte Carlo simulation method. The Monte Carlo simulation method requires the use of highly subjective assumptions. Our key assumptions in the method include the price and the expected volatility of our stock and our self-determined peer group of companies&#8217; (the "Peer Group") stock, risk free rate of return, dividend yields and cross-correlations between the Company and our Peer Group.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">Stock-based compensation is recognized on a straight-line basis over the requisite service periods of the stock awards, which is generally the vesting period.&#160;Compensation expense is recorded as a component of contract drilling services operating expenses and selling, general and administrative expenses in the Consolidated Statements of Operations. See </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">Note 11&#8212;Stock-based Compensation</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> for additional discussion on stock-based compensation. </span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:16px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Treasury Stock</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">Treasury stock purchases are accounted for under the cost method whereby the cost of the acquired stock is recorded as treasury stock.&#160;Gains and losses on the subsequent reissuance of shares are credited or charged to additional paid-in capital using the average-cost method. The stock to be offered pursuant to the grant of an award under the Helmerich &amp; Payne, Inc. 2016 Omnibus Incentive Plan may be authorized as treasury shares.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:16px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Comprehensive Income or Loss</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">Other comprehensive income or loss refers to revenues, expenses, gains, and losses that are included in comprehensive income or loss but excluded from net income or loss. We report the components of other comprehensive income or loss, net of tax, by their nature and disclose the tax effect allocated to each component in the Consolidated Statements of Comprehensive Income (Loss).&#160;</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:16px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Leases</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">We lease office space and equipment for use in operations. Leases are evaluated at inception or upon any subsequent material modification and, depending on the lease terms, are classified as either capital leases or operating leases as appropriate under ASC 840,</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:9pt;"> </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Leases</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">. For operating leases that contain built-in pre-determined rent escalations, rent expense is recognized on a straight-line basis over the life of the lease. Leasehold improvements are capitalized and amortized over the lease term. We do not have significant capital leases.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:16px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Recently Issued Accounting Updates</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">Changes to U.S. GAAP are established by the Financial Accounting Standards Board (&#8220;FASB&#8221;) in the form of ASUs to the FASB ASC. ASUs not listed below were assessed and determined to be either not applicable or clarifications of ASUs listed below.</span></div><div This was an exception to the principle in ASC 740, Income Taxes, that generally requires comprehensive recognition of current and deferred income taxes. The new guidance eliminates the exception for all intra-entity sales of assets other than inventory. As a result, a reporting entity recognizes the tax expense from the sale of the asset in the seller's tax jurisdiction when the transfer occurs, even though the pre-tax effects of that transaction are eliminated in consolidation. Any deferred tax asset that arises in the buyer's jurisdiction is also recognized at the time of the transfer. The new guidance does not apply to intra-entity transfers of inventory. The income tax consequences from the sale of inventory from one member of a consolidated entity to another will continue to be deferred until the inventory is sold to a third party.</span></div></td><td style="vertical-align:top;padding-left:2px;padding-top:2px;padding-bottom:2px;padding-right:2px;border-left:1px solid #000000;border-top:1px solid #000000;"><div style="text-align:left;padding-left:12px;font-size:8pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:8pt;">October 1, 2018</span></div></td><td style="vertical-align:top;padding-left:2px;padding-top:2px;padding-bottom:2px;padding-right:2px;border-left:1px solid #000000;border-right:1px solid #000000;border-top:1px solid #000000;"><div style="text-align:left;padding-left:12px;font-size:8pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:8pt;">We adopted this ASU during the first quarter of fiscal year 2019, as required. from the beginning balance of accumulated other comprehensive income.</span></div></td></tr></table></div></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:16px;font-size:10pt;"><div style="text-align:left;font-size:8pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:8pt;font-weight:bold;">Effect&#160;on&#160;the&#160;Financial&#160;Statements or&#160;Other Significant Matters</span></div></td></tr><tr><td style="vertical-align:top;background-color:#ccecff;padding-left:2px;padding-top:2px;padding-bottom:2px;padding-right:2px;border-left:1px solid #000000;border-top:1px solid #000000;"><div style="text-align:left;padding-left:12px;font-size:8pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:8pt;">ASU No. 2014-09, Revenue from Contracts with Customers (Topic 606)</span></div></td><td style="vertical-align:top;background-color:#ccecff;padding-left:2px;padding-top:2px;padding-bottom:2px;padding-right:2px;border-left:1px solid #000000;border-top:1px solid #000000;"><div style="text-align:left;padding-left:12px;font-size:8pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:8pt;">In May 2014, the FASB issued ASU No. 2014-09, Revenue from Contracts with Customers (Topic 606) (&#8220;ASC 606&#8221;). The update outlined a single comprehensive model for companies to use in accounting for revenue arising from contracts with customers and superseded other revenue recognition guidance, including industry-specific guidance. The core principle of the guidance is that an entity should recognize revenue when promised goods or services are transferred to customers in an amount that reflects the consideration to which the entity expects to be entitled for those goods or services. The update also required disclosures enabling users of financial statements to understand the nature, amount, timing and uncertainty of revenue and cash flows arising from contracts with customers. Furthermore, as part of Topic 606, the FASB introduced ASC 340-40, Other Assets and Deferred Costs, which provides guidance on the capitalization of contract related costs that are not within the scope of other authoritative literature. Companies could use either a full retrospective or a modified retrospective approach to adopt the updates.</span></div></td><td style="vertical-align:top;background-color:#ccecff;padding-left:2px;padding-top:2px;padding-bottom:2px;padding-right:2px;border-left:1px solid #000000;border-top:1px solid #000000;"><div style="text-align:left;padding-left:12px;font-size:8pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:8pt;">October 1, 2018</span></div></td><td style="vertical-align:top;background-color:#ccecff;padding-left:2px;padding-top:2px;padding-bottom:2px;padding-right:2px;border-left:1px solid #000000;border-right:1px solid #000000;border-top:1px solid #000000;"><div style="text-align:left;padding-left:12px;font-size:8pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:8pt;">We adopted this topic, using the modified retrospective transitional approach, during the first quarter of fiscal year 2019, as required. We recognized the cumulative effect by initially applying the revenue standard as an adjustment to the opening balance of retained earnings during the period (October 1, 2018). Refer to Note 10&#8212;Revenue from Contracts with Customers for the impact of the adoption.</span></div></td></tr><tr><td style="vertical-align:top;padding-left:2px;padding-top:2px;padding-bottom:2px;padding-right:2px;border-left:1px solid #000000;border-top:1px solid #000000;"><div style="text-align:left;padding-left:12px;font-size:8pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:8pt;">ASU No. 2018-13, Fair Value Measurement (Topic 820): Disclosure Framework &#8211; &#160;Changes to the Disclosure Requirements for Fair Value Measurement</span></div></td><td style="vertical-align:top;padding-left:2px;padding-top:2px;padding-bottom:2px;padding-right:2px;border-left:1px solid #000000;border-top:1px solid #000000;"><div style="text-align:left;padding-left:12px;font-size:8pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:8pt;">This ASU eliminates, adds and modifies certain disclosure requirements for fair value measurements as part of the FASB&#8217;s disclosure framework project, where entities will no longer be required to disclose the amount of and reasons for transfers between Level 1 and Level 2 of the fair value hierarchy, but public companies will be required to disclose the range and weighted average used to develop significant unobservable inputs for Level 3 fair value measurements. This update is effective for annual and interim periods beginning after December 15, 2019. Early adoption is permitted. <br/>&#160;</span></div></td><td style="vertical-align:top;padding-left:2px;padding-top:2px;padding-bottom:2px;padding-right:2px;border-left:1px solid #000000;border-top:1px solid #000000;"><div style="text-align:left;padding-left:12px;font-size:8pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:8pt;">June 30, 2019</span></div></td><td style="vertical-align:top;padding-left:2px;padding-top:2px;padding-bottom:2px;padding-right:2px;border-left:1px solid #000000;border-right:1px solid #000000;border-top:1px solid #000000;"><div style="text-align:left;padding-left:12px;font-size:8pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:8pt;">We early adopted this ASU during the third quarter of fiscal year 2019. The adoption did not have a material impact to our consolidated financial statements and disclosures. Refer to Note 13&#8212;Fair Value Measurement of Financial Instruments. </span></div></td></tr><tr><td style="vertical-align:top;background-color:#cceeff;padding-left:2px;padding-top:2px;padding-bottom:2px;padding-right:2px;border-left:1px solid #000000;border-top:1px solid #000000;"><div style="text-align:left;padding-left:12px;font-size:8pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:8pt;">ASU No. 2018-02, Income Statement &#8211; Reporting Comprehensive Income (Topic 220) Reclassification of Certain Tax Effects From Accumulated Other Comprehensive Income</span></div></td><td style="vertical-align:top;background-color:#cceeff;padding-left:2px;padding-top:2px;padding-bottom:2px;padding-right:2px;border-left:1px solid #000000;border-top:1px solid #000000;"><div style="text-align:left;padding-left:12px;font-size:8pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:8pt;">This ASU relates to the impacts of the Tax Reform Act. The guidance permits the reclassification of certain income tax effects of the Tax Reform Act from Accumulated Other Comprehensive Income (Loss) to Retained Earnings. The guidance also requires certain new disclosures. This update is effective for fiscal years beginning after December 15, 2018, and interim periods within those fiscal periods and early adoption is permitted. Entities may adopt the guidance using one of two transition methods, retrospective to each period (or periods) in which the income tax effects of the Tax Reform Act related to the items remaining in Other Comprehensive Income are recognized or at the beginning of the period of adoption.</span></div></td><td style="vertical-align:top;background-color:#cceeff;padding-left:2px;padding-top:2px;padding-bottom:2px;padding-right:2px;border-left:1px solid #000000;border-top:1px solid #000000;"><div style="text-align:left;padding-left:12px;font-size:8pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:8pt;">June 30, 2019</span></div></td><td style="vertical-align:top;background-color:#cceeff;padding-left:2px;padding-top:2px;padding-bottom:2px;padding-right:2px;border-left:1px solid #000000;border-right:1px solid #000000;border-top:1px solid #000000;"><div style="text-align:left;padding-left:12px;font-size:8pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:8pt;">We early adopted this ASU during the third quarter of fiscal year 2019. companies in the oil and gas industry, may impact credit risk as customers may be similarly affected by prolonged changes in economic and industry conditions.&#160;&#160;International sales also present various risks including governmental activities that may limit or disrupt markets and restrict the movement of funds.&#160;&#160;Most of our international sales, however, are to large international or government-owned national oil companies.&#160;&#160;We perform credit evaluations of customers and do not typically require collateral in support for trade receivables.&#160;&#160;We provide an allowance for doubtful accounts, when necessary, to cover estimated credit losses.&#160;&#160;Such an allowance is based on management&#8217;s knowledge of customer accounts.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:16px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Volatility of Market</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">Our operations can be materially affected by oil and gas prices.&#160;&#160;Oil and natural gas prices have been historically volatile and difficult to predict with any degree of certainty.&#160;&#160;While current energy prices are important contributors to positive cash flow for customers, expectations about future prices and price volatility are generally more important for determining a customer&#8217;s future spending levels.&#160;&#160;This volatility, along with the difficulty in predicting future prices, can lead many exploration and production companies to base their capital spending on more conservative estimates of commodity prices.&#160;&#160;As a result, demand for contract drilling services is not always purely a function of the movement of commodity prices.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">In addition, customers may finance their exploration activities through cash flow from operations, the incurrence of debt or the issuance of equity.&#160;&#160;Any deterioration in the credit and capital markets may cause difficulty for customers to obtain funding for their capital needs.&#160;&#160;A reduction of cash flow resulting from declines in commodity prices or a reduction of available financing may result in a reduction in customer spending and the demand for our services.&#160;&#160;This reduction in spending could have a material adverse effect on our operations.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;font-size:9pt;"><span probable.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">We self-insure a significant portion of expected Generally, deductibles range from </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$1 million</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> to </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$5 million</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> per occurrence depending on the coverage and whether a claim occurs outside or inside of the United States. Insurance is purchased over deductibles to reduce our exposure to catastrophic events. Estimates are recorded for incurred outstanding liabilities for workers&#8217; compensation, general liability claims and claims that are incurred but not reported. Estimates are based on adjusters&#8217; estimates, historical experience and statistical methods commonly used within the insurance industry that we believe are reliable.&#160;We have also engaged a third-party actuary to perform a review of our domestic casualty losses.&#160;&#160;Nonetheless, insurance estimates include certain assumptions and management judgments regarding the frequency and severity of claims, claim development and settlement practices. Unanticipated changes in these factors may produce materially different amounts of expense that would be reported under these programs.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:16px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">International Land Drilling Operations</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">International Land drilling operations may significantly contribute to our revenues and net operating income.&#160;There can be no assurance that we will be able to successfully conduct such operations, and a failure to do so may have an adverse effect on our financial position, results of operations, and cash flows.&#160;&#160;Also, the success of our international land operations will be subject to numerous contingencies, some of which are beyond management&#8217;s control.&#160;&#160;These contingencies include general and regional economic conditions, fluctuations in currency exchange rates, modified exchange controls, changes in international regulatory requirements and international employment issues, risk of expropriation of real and personal property and the burden of complying with foreign laws.&#160;&#160;Additionally, in the event that extended labor strikes occur or a country experiences significant political, economic or social instability, we could experience shortages in labor and/or material and supplies necessary to operate some of our drilling rigs, thereby potentially causing an adverse material effect on our business, financial condition and results of operations. In Argentina, while our dayrate is denominated in U.S. dollars, we are paid in Argentine pesos.&#160;&#160;The Argentine branch of one of our second-tier subsidiaries remits U.S. dollars to its U.S. parent by converting the Argentine pesos into U.S. dollars through the Argentine Foreign Exchange Market and repatriating the U.S. dollars.&#160;Argentina also has a history of implementing currency controls, which restrict the conversion and repatriation of U.S. dollars, including controls which were implemented in September 2019 and are presently in effect. As a result of these currency controls, our ability to remit funds from our Argentine subsidiary to its U.S. parent has been limited.  Furthermore, the Argentine government has also instituted price controls on crude oil, diesel and gasoline prices and instituted an exchange rate freeze in connection with those prices.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">Argentina&#8217;s economy is considered highly inflationary, which is defined as cumulative inflation rates exceeding </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>100 percent</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> in the most recent </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">three-year</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> period based on inflation data published by the respective governments.&#160;&#160;Nonetheless, all of our foreign subsidiaries use the U.S. dollar as the functional currency and local currency monetary assets and liabilities are remeasured into U.S. dollars with gains and losses resulting from foreign currency transactions included in current results of operations.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span to&#160;</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;color:#212529;"><span>9.6 percent</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;color:#212529;">&#160;during the&#160;year During the&#160;year ended&#160;</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;color:#212529;">September&#160;30, 2019</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;color:#212529;">, approximately&#160;</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;color:#212529;"><span>91.6 percent</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;color:#212529;">&#160;of operating revenues from international locations were from operations in South America compared to&#160;</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;color:#212529;"><span>96.0 percent</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;color:#212529;">&#160;during the&#160;year ended&#160;</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;color:#212529;">September&#160;30, 2018</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;color:#212529;">. Substantially all of the South American operating revenues were from Argentina and Colombia. The future occurrence of one or more international events arising from the types of risks described above could have a material adverse impact on our business, financial condition and results of operations.</span></div><span></span>

<tr><td><div class="body" style="padding: 2px;">
<a href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.toggleNext( this );">- Definition</a><div><p>The entire disclosure for the organization, consolidation and basis of presentation of financial statements disclosure, and significant accounting policies of the reporting entity. May be provided in more than one note to the financial statements, as long as users are provided with an understanding of (1) the significant judgments and assumptions made by an enterprise in determining whether it must consolidate a VIE and/or disclose information about its involvement with a VIE, (2) the nature of restrictions on a consolidated VIE's assets reported by an enterprise in its statement of financial position, including the carrying amounts of such assets, (3) the nature of, and changes in, the risks associated with an enterprise's involvement with the VIE, and (4) how an enterprise's involvement with the VIE affects the enterprise's financial position, financial performance, and cash flows.  Describes procedure if disclosures are provided in more than one note to the financial statements.</p></div>

style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;color:#252525;"><span>$7.0 million</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;color:#252525;">&#160;for each of the next three succeeding fiscal years, approximately </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;color:#252525;"><span>$6.4 million</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;color:#252525;">&#160;for&#160;fiscal year 2023 and approximately </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;color:#252525;"><span>$6.2 million</span></span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"> </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;color:#252525;">for fiscal year 2024</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;color:#252525;">.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:16px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;">Impairments</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">During the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2018, and as part of our annual goodwill impairment test, we performed a detailed assessment of the </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;color:#252525;">TerraVici</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> reporting unit, where </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$4.7 million</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> of goodwill was allocated. We determined that the estimated fair value of this reporting unit was less than its carrying amount and we recorded goodwill impairment losses of </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$4.7 million</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> (</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$3.5 million</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, net of tax, or </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$0.03</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> per diluted share). &#160;In addition, we recorded an intangible assets impairment loss of </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$0.9 million</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> (</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$0.7 million</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> net of tax, or </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$0.01</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> per diluted share). These impairment losses&#160;are </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;color:#252525;">included</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> in Asset Impairment Charge on the Consolidated Statements of Operations for the&#160;fiscal year ended September&#160;30, 2018. Our goodwill impairment analysis performed on our remaining technology reporting units in the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2018 did not result in an impairment charge. </span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">Beginning October 1, 2018, the goodwill associated with our technology reporting units were combined into one reporting unit, H&amp;P Technologies.  Our goodwill impairment analysis performed in the fourth quarter fiscal year of 2019 indicated that the fair value of the H&amp;P Technologies reporting unit exceeded its carrying value. Therefore, no goodwill impairment was recognized.</span></div><span></span>
</td>

style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"/><span income includes&#160;a tax benefit of approximately&#160;</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$502.1 million</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, or </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$4.59</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> per share on a diluted basis, an after-tax gain from the sale of assets of&#160;</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$4.2 million</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, or </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$0.04</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> per share on a diluted basis. In the second quarter of fiscal year </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">2018</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, net loss includes an after-tax gain from the sale of assets of </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$3.8 million</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, or </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$0.04</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> per share on a diluted basis. In the third quarter of fiscal year </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">2018</span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, net loss includes an after-tax gain from the sale of assets of </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$3.1 million</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;">, or </span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"><span>$0.02</span></span><span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"> per share on a diluted basis. Certain other corporate activities, our real estate operations and our incubator program for new research and development projects are included in "Other". All segment disclosures have been restated for these segment changes. Specifically, income and expenses of a subsidiary acquired or disposed of during the fiscal year are included in the consolidated statement of profit or loss and other comprehensive income from the date the Company gains control until the date when the Company ceases to control the subsidiary. All significant intercompany accounts and transactions have been eliminated in consolidation. &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:16px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;Foreign Currencies&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;Our functional currency, together with all our foreign subsidiaries, is the U.S. dollar. style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;Inventories of Materials and Supplies&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;Inventories are primarily replacement parts and supplies held for consumption in our drilling operations. Inventories are valued at the lower of cost or net realizable value. Cost is determined on a weighted average basis and includes the cost of materials, shipping, duties and labor. Net realizable value is defined as the estimated selling price in the ordinary course of business, less reasonably predictable costs of completion, disposal and transportation. The reserves for excess and obsolete inventory were &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$11.5 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$9.9 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; for fiscal years &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;2019&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;2018&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, respectively.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:16px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;Investments&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;We maintain investments in equity securities of certain publicly traded companies. We recognize our marketable equity securities that have readily determinable fair values at fair value, with changes in such values reflected in net income. We adopted ASU No. 2016-01 on October 1, 2018, and as a result, we recognize our marketable equity securities that have readily determinable fair values at fair value, with changes in such values reflected in net income.&#160;Previously, we recognized changes in fair value of equity securities in other comprehensive income in the Consolidated Statements of Comprehensive Income (Loss). There is no longer a requirement to consider whether the decline in fair value is other-than-temporary. &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:16px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;Property, Plant, and Equipment&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;Property, plant and equipment are stated at cost less accumulated depreciation. Substantially all property, plant and equipment are depreciated using the straight-line method based on the estimated useful lives of the assets after deducting their salvage values. The amount of depreciation expense we record is dependent upon certain assumptions, including an asset&#x2019;s estimated useful life,&#160;rate of consumption, and corresponding salvage value. We periodically review these assumptions and may change one or more of these assumptions. Changes in our assumptions may require us to recognize, on a prospective basis, increased or decreased depreciation expense.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;We capitalize interest on major projects during construction. Interest is capitalized based on the average interest rate on related debt. We had &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;no&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; capitalized interest for fiscal year &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;2019&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$0.4 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$0.3 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; of capitalized interest for &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;2018&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;2017&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, respectively.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;We review long-lived assets for impairment whenever events or changes in circumstances indicate that the carrying amount of an asset may not be recoverable.&#160;Changes that could prompt such an assessment include a significant decline in revenue or cash margin per day, extended periods of low rig asset group utilization, changes in market demand for a specific asset, obsolescence, completion of specific contracts, restructuring of our drilling fleet, and/or overall general market conditions.&#160;&#160;If the review of the long-lived assets indicates that the carrying value of these assets/asset groups&#160;is more than the estimated undiscounted future cash flows projected to be realized from the use of the asset and its eventual disposal&#160;an impairment charge is made, as required, to adjust the carrying value down to the estimated fair value of the asset.&#160;&#160;The estimated fair value is determined based upon either an income approach using estimated discounted future cash flows, a market approach considering factors such as recent market sales of rigs of other companies and our own sales of rigs, appraisals and other factors, a cost approach utilizing reproduction costs new as adjusted for the asset age and condition, and/or a combination of multiple approaches.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;Cash flows are estimated by management considering factors such as prospective market demand, margins, recent changes in rig technology and its effect on each rig&#x2019;s marketability, any investment required to make a rig operational, suitability of rig size and make up to existing platforms, and competitive dynamics including industry utilization.&#160;Long-lived assets that are held for sale are recorded at the lower of carrying value or the fair value less costs to sell.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:16px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;Goodwill and Intangible Assets&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;color:#252525;"&gt;Goodwill represents the excess of purchase price over the fair value of net assets acquired in a business combination, at the date of acquisition. Goodwill is not amortized but is tested for potential impairment at the reporting unit level at a minimum on an annual basis in the fourth fiscal quarter of each fiscal year or when it is more likely than not that the carrying value may exceed fair value. If an impairment is determined to exist, an &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;impairment &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;color:#252525;"&gt;charge for the amount by which the carrying amount exceeds the reporting unit&#x2019;s fair value is recognized, limited to the total amount of goodwill allocated to that reporting unit.&#160;&#160;The reporting unit level is defined as an operating segment or one level below an operating segment.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;color:#252525;"&gt;Finite-lived intangible assets are amortized &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;using&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;color:#252525;"&gt; the straight-line method over the period in which these assets contribute to our cash flows, generally estimated to be &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;color:#252525;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;5&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;color:#252525;"&gt; to &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;color:#252525;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;20 years&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;color:#252525;"&gt; and are evaluated for impairment in accordance with our policies for valuation of long-lived assets.&#160;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:16px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;Drilling Revenues&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;Contract drilling services revenues are comprised of daywork drilling contracts for which the related revenues and expenses are recognized as services are performed and collection is reasonably assured.&#160;&#160;For certain contracts, we receive payments contractually designated for the mobilization of rigs and other drilling equipment.&#160;&#160;Mobilization payments received, and direct costs incurred for the mobilization, are deferred and recognized on a straight-line basis as the drilling service is provided.&#160;&#160;Costs incurred to relocate rigs and other drilling equipment to areas in which a contract has not been secured are expensed as incurred.&#160;&#160;Reimbursements received for out-of-pocket expenses are recorded as both revenues and direct costs.&#160;Reimbursements for fiscal years &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;2019&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;2018&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;2017&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; were &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$322.8 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$274.7 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$179.9 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, respectively.&#160;For contracts that are terminated by customers prior to the expirations of their fixed terms, contractual provisions customarily require early termination amounts to be paid to us.&#160;&#160;Revenues from early terminated contracts are recognized when all contractual requirements have been met.&#160;Early termination revenue for fiscal years &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;2019&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;2018&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;2017&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; was approximately &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$11.3 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$17.1 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$29.4 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, respectively.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:16px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;Rent Revenues&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;We enter into leases with tenants in our rental properties consisting primarily of retail and multi-tenant warehouse space.&#160;The lease terms of tenants occupying space in the retail centers and warehouse buildings generally range from &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;three&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; to &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;ten years&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;. Minimum rents are recognized on a straight-line basis over the term of the related leases.&#160;&#160;Overage and percentage rents are based on tenants&#x2019; sales volume.&#160;&#160;Recoveries from #000000;padding-left:2px;padding-top:2px;padding-bottom:2px;background-color:#cceeff;border-top:1px solid #000000;"&gt;&lt;div style="text-align:left;font-size:8pt;"&gt;&lt;span #000000;background-color:#cceeff;padding-top:2px;padding-bottom:2px;border-top:1px solid #000000;"&gt;&lt;div style="text-align:right;font-size:8pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:8pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;26,861&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:bottom;border-bottom:3px double #000000;background-color:#cceeff;border-top:1px solid #000000;"&gt;&lt;div style="text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:16px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;Income Taxes&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;Current income tax expense is the amount of income taxes expected to be payable for the current fiscal year.&#160;&#160;Deferred income taxes are computed using the liability method and are provided on all temporary differences between the financial basis and the tax basis of our assets and liabilities.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;We provide for uncertain tax positions when such tax positions do not meet the recognition thresholds or measurement standards prescribed in Accounting Standards Codification (&#x201c;ASC&#x201d;) 740,&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:9pt;"&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;Income Taxes&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, which is more fully discussed in &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;Note 8&#x2014;Income Taxes&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;.&#160;&#160;Amounts for uncertain tax positions are adjusted in periods when new information becomes available or when positions are effectively settled.&#160;&#160;We recognize accrued interest related to unrecognized tax benefits in interest expense and penalties in other expense in the Consolidated Statements of Operations.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:16px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;Earnings per Common Share&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;Basic earnings per share is computed utilizing the two-class method and is calculated based on the weighted-average number of common shares outstanding during the periods presented. Diluted earnings per share is computed using the weighted-average number of common and common equivalent shares outstanding during the periods utilizing the two-class method for stock options and nonvested restricted stock. We have granted and expect to continue to grant to employees restricted stock grants that contain non-forfeitable rights to dividends. Such grants are considered participating securities under ASC 260,&#160;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;Earnings Per Share&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;. As such, we have included these grants in the calculation of our basic earnings per share.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:16px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;Stock-Based Compensation&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;Stock-based compensation expense is determined using a fair-value-based measurement method for all awards granted.&#160;During the fiscal year ended September&#160;30, 2019, there were no new non-qualified stock options granted, as we have, prospectively and for fiscal year 2019, replaced stock options with performance share units as a component of our executives&#x2019; long-term equity incentive compensation. We have also eliminated stock options as an element of our director compensation program. The Board has determined to award stock-based compensation to directors solely in the form of restricted stock. &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;The fair value of each option granted in prior years was estimated on the date of grant based on the Black-Scholes options-pricing model utilizing assumptions for a risk-free interest rate, volatility, dividend yield and expected remaining term of the awards.&#160;The assumptions used in calculating the fair value of stock-based payment awards represent management&#x2019;s best estimates, but these estimates involve inherent uncertainties and the application of management judgment.&#160;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;The grant date fair value of performance share units is determined through use of the Monte Carlo simulation method. The Monte Carlo simulation method requires the use of highly subjective assumptions. Our key assumptions in the method include the price and the expected volatility of our stock and our self-determined peer group of companies&#x2019; (the "Peer Group") stock, risk free rate of return, dividend yields and cross-correlations between the Company and our Peer Group.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;Stock-based compensation is recognized on a straight-line basis over the requisite service periods of the stock awards, which is generally the vesting period.&#160;Compensation expense is recorded as a component of contract drilling services operating expenses and selling, general and administrative expenses in the Consolidated Statements of Operations. See &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;Note 11&#x2014;Stock-based Compensation&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; for additional discussion on stock-based compensation. &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:16px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;Treasury Stock&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;Treasury stock purchases are accounted for under the cost method whereby the cost of the acquired stock is recorded as treasury stock.&#160;Gains and losses on the subsequent reissuance of shares are credited or charged to additional paid-in capital using the average-cost method. The stock to be offered pursuant to the grant of an award under the Helmerich &amp;amp; Payne, Inc. 2016 Omnibus Incentive Plan may be authorized as treasury shares.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:16px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;Comprehensive Income or Loss&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;Other comprehensive income or loss refers to revenues, expenses, gains, and losses that are included in comprehensive income or loss but excluded from net income or loss. We report the components of other comprehensive income or loss, net of tax, by their nature and disclose the tax effect allocated to each component in the Consolidated Statements of Comprehensive Income (Loss).&#160;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:16px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;Leases&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;We lease office space and equipment for use in operations. Leases are evaluated at inception or upon any subsequent material modification and, depending on the lease terms, are classified as either capital leases or operating leases as appropriate under ASC 840,&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:9pt;"&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;Leases&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;. For operating leases that contain built-in pre-determined rent escalations, rent expense is recognized on a straight-line basis over the life of the lease. Leasehold improvements are capitalized and amortized over the lease term. We do not have significant capital leases.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:16px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;Recently Issued Accounting Updates&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;Changes to U.S. GAAP are established by the Financial Accounting Standards Board (&#x201c;FASB&#x201d;) in the form of ASUs to the FASB ASC. We consider the applicability and impact of all ASUs. ASUs not listed below were assessed and determined to be either not applicable or clarifications of ASUs listed below.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="text-align:left;padding-left:12px;font-size:8pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:8pt;"&gt;Under the new guidance, modification accounting is required only if the fair value, the vesting conditions, or the classification of the award (as equity or liability) changes as a result of the change in terms or conditions. Regardless of whether the change to the terms or conditions of the award requires modification accounting, the existing disclosure requirements and other aspects of U.S. GAAP associated with modification, such as earnings per share, continue to apply.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;background-color:#ccecff;padding-left:2px;padding-top:2px;padding-bottom:2px;padding-right:2px;border-left:1px solid #000000;border-top:1px solid #000000;"&gt;&lt;div style="text-align:left;padding-left:12px;font-size:8pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:8pt;"&gt;October 1, 2018&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;background-color:#ccecff;padding-left:2px;padding-top:2px;padding-bottom:2px;padding-right:2px;border-left:1px solid #000000;border-right:1px solid #000000;border-top:1px solid #000000;"&gt;&lt;div style="text-align:left;padding-left:12px;font-size:8pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:8pt;"&gt;We adopted this ASU during the first quarter of fiscal year 2019, as required. There was no impact to our consolidated financial statements and disclosures.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;padding-left:2px;padding-top:2px;padding-bottom:2px;padding-right:2px;border-left:1px solid #000000;border-top:1px solid #000000;border-bottom:1px solid #000000;"&gt;&lt;div style="text-align:left;padding-left:12px;font-size:8pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:8pt;"&gt;ASU No. 2017-07, Compensation &#x2013; Retirement Benefits (Topic 715): Improving the Presentation of Net Periodic Pension Cost and Net Periodic Postretirement Benefit Cost&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;padding-left:2px;padding-top:2px;padding-bottom:2px;padding-right:2px;border-left:1px solid #000000;border-top:1px solid #000000;border-bottom:1px solid #000000;"&gt;&lt;div style="text-align:left;padding-left:12px;font-size:8pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:8pt;"&gt;The ASU changes how employers that sponsor defined benefit pension and/or other postretirement benefit plans present the net periodic benefit cost in the income statement. Employers should present the service cost component of net periodic benefit cost in the same income statement line item(s) as other employee compensation costs arising from services rendered during the period. Employers should present the other components of the net periodic benefit cost separately from the line item(s) that includes the service cost and outside of any subtotal of operating income, if one is presented. The amendments are applied retrospectively for the presentation of the service cost component and other components of net periodic pension cost and net periodic postretirement benefit cost in the income statement.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;padding-left:2px;padding-top:2px;padding-bottom:2px;padding-right:2px;border-left:1px solid #000000;border-top:1px solid #000000;border-bottom:1px solid #000000;"&gt;&lt;div style="text-align:left;padding-left:12px;font-size:8pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:8pt;"&gt;October 1, 2018&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;padding-left:2px;padding-top:2px;padding-bottom:2px;padding-right:2px;border-left:1px solid #000000;border-right:1px solid #000000;border-top:1px solid #000000;border-bottom:1px solid #000000;"&gt;&lt;div style="text-align:left;padding-left:12px;font-size:8pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:8pt;"&gt;We adopted this ASU during the first quarter of fiscal year 2019, as required, on a retrospective basis. The retrospective impact was not material to our consolidated financial statements and disclosures. &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div
